Definition: from G3631 and a form of the base of G5397; an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness):--excess of wine.
BiblicalUsage: Oinophlygia is excess of wine, drunkenness, the overflow of the cup. It occurs once, in 1 Peter 4:3, in the list of the Gentiles' old life: lasciviousness, lusts, excess of wine, revellings, banquetings, and abominable idolatries.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe excess of wine belongs to the old life, and the time past is enough for the will of the Gentiles.
